findings.reason: the plan should re-frame §2 as extending the existing helper and the `if local` guard at reckon/crew/picker/snapshot.py:817, which shrinks the node and avoids a drifting second reader.
findings.text: §2 describes reading `admission.sessions[session].worker_slots` then `new_session_worker_slots` then the global as new work, but `_lane_worker_allowance` already implements that precedence and the picker already calls it at reckon/crew/picker/snapshot.py:272; a second rendering would be a fork

findings.reason: §4's queued-run clause should name this owner and extend it rather than describe a second path.
findings.text: §4 proposes re-composing a queued run's launch from the recorded node, which `_launch_queued` already does (it rebuilds the node via `_node_from_pointer` and forwards the pointer's `dispatch_options` to `dispatch`), and the plan does not cite it

findings.reason: naming the owner turns §2 into a one-site extension and prevents two readers of the queued admission block diverging.
findings.text: §2's per-session slot reading is a duplicate of the shared state reader `_lane_worker_allowance` in this file; the plan names no owner, so the author may add a parallel reader beside the one the picker already trusts

findings.reason: the queued-move behaviour should extend this owner, which already carries `dispatch_options` and `_node_from_pointer`, instead of forking a second launch recomposition.
findings.text: §4's "moved by re-composing its launch from the recorded node" duplicates the pointer-to-launch path `_launch_queued`; the plan names no owner

findings.reason: the section must state that these options mirror the fields `dispatch` already passes (existing inputs restated on a second command, not net-new interface) or name the option it replaces.
findings.text: §3 adds write paths, negative control, estimated hours and section as `crew pick` options (a `cli_options` family that this week stands at 350) and the section names neither what it retires or merges nor why nothing can be, so the added surface is unaccounted for in its own text

rubric_items.deep_module: pass — the mechanism §2 needs is already one deep helper (`_lane_worker_allowance`) that hides the admission-map shape, the session precedence and the headroom fallback; §2's addition is a guard-rail and guidance, not a new surface spread over many wrappers.
rubric_items.duplicate_owner: a finding — §2 duplicates the session-slot state reader owned by `reckon/crew/dispatch_plan.py:_lane_worker_allowance`, and §4 duplicates the pointer-to-launch recomposition owned by `reckon/crew/queue_admission.py:_launch_queued`.
rubric_items.interface_budget: a finding — public_definitions 1724, cli_options 350, mcp_views 34, refusal_families 23; §3 adds CLI options to `crew pick` without naming what it retires or merges, or why nothing can be.
rubric_items.reuse_search: a finding — the plan re-describes machinery that already exists and cites neither: the session-slot reader `_lane_worker_allowance` (reckon/crew/dispatch_plan.py:1157, already called by the picker at reckon/crew/picker/snapshot.py:272) and the queued-launch recomposition `_launch_queued` (reckon/crew/queue_admission.py:142).
rubric_items.thin_wrapper: pass — no wrapper is proposed; §3 extends the existing `crew pick` command and §4 would extend the existing `change_lane`, both extensions of owners rather than parallel thin layers.
